message.content: {"calls":[{"tool":"chest_xray_expert","args":{"question":"In this lateral chest X-ray, there is a linear radiopaque structure consistent with an indwelling catheter. Based on the 'L' marker indicating the left side of the patient (posterior aspect in standard lateral view), and the position of the catheter relative to the spine and sternum, which side is the catheter most likely located? Note: In a standard lateral CXR, the left side is typically posterior (near spine) and right side anterior (near sternum) if marked L posteriorly, OR the marker indicates the side facing the detector. Please analyze the catheter's trajectory and depth."}}],"reason":"To get a more nuanced analysis from the expert model regarding catheter laterality in a lateral view, specifically asking it to reason about anatomical depth relative to the orientation marker rather than just guessing a side."}
